title: Stability bounded by a stable influence
statement: Let $g$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube and let $\rho\in[0,1]$. Form a Boolean function on the $(n+1)$-dimensional sign cube by multiplying the first coordinate by $g$ evaluated on the remaining coordinates. The stability curve of the real-valued version of $g$ at $\rho$ is at most the stable influence of this new function in its first coordinate, where stable influence weights each squared Fourier coefficient containing that coordinate by $\rho$ raised to one less than the size of its index set.
hypotheses_covered: $g$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
